headline: How to Prepare for a Small Bathroom Renovation Project
articleBody:
Preparing for a small bathroom overhaul requires thoughtful planning because tight quarters leave zero margin for measurement errors or uncoordinated trades. Use this practical preparation list before demolition begins:

- [ ] Measure total room dimensions and ceiling height — Confirms exact square footage so material orders for tile, drywall, and paint are accurate.
- [ ] Check door swing clearances for the entry and vanity — Ensures the main room door and under-sink cabinets open freely without striking fixtures.
- [ ] Verify toilet clearance space — Confirms at least fifteen inches from the toilet centerline to adjacent side walls or vanity panels to meet code.
- [ ] Confirm vanity depth and plumbing rough-in locations — Prevents ordering a cabinet that protrudes into walking paths or blocks existing supply valves.
- [ ] Inspect existing exhaust fan ducting — Ensures ventilation vents directly to the outdoors rather than discharging humid air into the attic space.
- [ ] Select and order all primary fixtures in advance — Keeps faucets, valves, and tile on site so construction proceeds without waiting for deliveries.
- [ ] Confirm permit responsibilities with your contractor — Establishes who pulls building, plumbing, and electrical permits before structural work starts.

How to use this checklist:
Review these concrete items with your contractor during your initial on-site consultation. Addressing clearances, ventilation pathways, and fixture deliveries early keeps active construction within the expected four- to six-week timeframe.
